tasks.short: Apply a known mathematical technique and judge a nonstandard result.

steps.what: Name the mathematical technique for this derivative valuation.
Assemble market series for the chosen mathematical technique.

loop.input: Named technique and the market history it needs
loop.output: Series rows with instrument, date and value
loop.check: The analyst checks a sample of dates against the source
loop.stop: One pass; a date with no value stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: History arrives under different names, so a fixed column map misses series

steps.what: Apply the chosen statistical formula to the market series.
Judge a nonstandard derivative valuation or regulation result.
File the valuation result the analyst has accepted.

tasks.design: The analyst names the mathematical technique, and {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles the series that technique needs. A stored formula runs only for a technique already accepted. A nonstandard derivative valuation or a regulation result stays with the analyst, and only the checked reading is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The technique and the series lived in personal files, so a formula could not be reused without re-reading the question.
tasks.enabler_now: Series can be assembled once the technique and the fields are named. Choosing the technique, and reading a result the formula does not cover, cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A valuation whose market has no series, or a regulation question the formula was not built for.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows when the formula is the wrong tool for the question.
tasks.altitude: Series are ready before the reading. The analyst still chooses the technique and can refuse a result. Decision rights on the valuation do not move.

reach.task: Say which regulation questions must use a checked method
reach.learn: Which regulation questions a stored formula must not answer

evidence.claim: Choosing a mathematical technique for a derivative question stays with the analyst, because standard software does not cover the house models.
In a published spreadsheet-agent test, most models ended a cash waterfall at €1.16 million, not €580,000.
Credit scoring of natural persons is high-risk under annex III 5(b); firms fall outside that duty and sole traders do not.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. Boundary: from a valuation question to a filed reading. Trading the position is a later task.

Structured fields are technique, instrument, date, value and result. The analyst names the technique; the market history produces the values. Fallback: a blank date is not filled with zero, and the formula does not run.
Configure the series pull on {DATA_PLATFORM} before custom code.
Upkeep of 5 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new instrument field on the series.
A firm's derivative valuation is not credit scoring of a natural person. A sole trader as the subject would be the edge.
unknowns: Whether the house formula library already names techniques the same way the questions do.
Whether regulation questions are in this book or handled by another team.
research_questions: What share of questions use a technique already in the library?
How often is a formula result refused as the wrong tool?

incremental.description: Add an instrument field when a new market is in the book

approvals.approved_version: valuation reading the analyst accepted for this question

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the question is nonstandard, so the series and the formula are not used and the reading stays manual. High: the technique is known and only the assembly shrinks. The choice and the nonstandard reading stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Specify a portfolio tool, prototype it, and accept it on a known book.

steps.what: Specify the portfolio attribution the analytical tools must measure.
Prototype the pricing model on a known portfolio.

loop.input: Tool specification and a portfolio whose result is already known
loop.output: A small prototype that returns the named attribution
loop.check: The analyst compares the prototype total with the known portfolio result
loop.stop: Stop when the totals match or a missing input is listed
loop.why_not_simpler: The attribution definition is prose, so a fixed report cannot invent the measure

steps.what: Run the stored test for that pricing model.
Check the prototype result against the known portfolio.
Accept or refuse the analytical tool for library use.

tasks.design: The analyst specifies the portfolio attribution, and a prototype is tried on a book whose result is known. {DATA_PLATFORM} runs the stored test. Library acceptance stays with the analyst; deployment is the developer's work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tools were written as one-off files, so a known-book test was rebuilt each time.
tasks.enabler_now: A named measure can be prototyped and tested once the specification exists. Deciding the measure, and accepting the tool, cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A performance measure the known book does not contain.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows which difference is a bug and which is the point of the new measure.
tasks.altitude: Prototypes arrive with a test. The analyst still decides what the tool must measure, and can keep it out of the library. Decision rights on the measure do not move.

reach.task: Say which performance figures a client explanation may use
reach.learn: Which attribution figures are safe to repeat outside the desk

evidence.claim: Specifying a portfolio measure and accepting a tool stay with the analyst.
A stored comparison against a known book is a rules test once the expected total exists.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. The developer's deployment is not the analyst's saving. Boundary: from a measure question to a library decision. Using the tool on a live book is later.

Structured fields are measure name, portfolio id, expected total and test status. The analyst writes the measure; the known book produces the expected total. Fallback: a prototype with no expected total is not accepted.
Configure the stored test on {DATA_PLATFORM} before custom code.
Upkeep of 8 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new measure added to the test list.
unknowns: Whether a known book with an agreed total already exists.
Whether deployment is a separate developer or the analyst.
research_questions: What share of new tools have a known-book total before the prototype?
How often is a prototype refused?

incremental.description: Add a measure to the stored test list

approvals.approved_version: library decision on the prototype that matched the known portfolio

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: there is no known book, so the prototype and the test are done by hand and acceptance is unchanged. High: the book exists and only the test run shrinks. Specification and acceptance stay. Developer time is not saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Refresh financial results, tie them, and interpret the break.

steps.what: Refresh results of the financial analysis procedures.
Tie each financial result to its source row.
Interpret a break the financial analysis procedures do not explain.
Record the interpretation of the financial analysis.

tasks.design: {BI} refreshes the procedure results and ties each figure to a source row. The analyst interprets a break the tolerance does not explain. The recorded interpretation is the version the analyst has checked.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were copied into a note, so a break could not be traced to the row that caused it.
tasks.enabler_now: A refresh and a tie-out are rules once procedures and source rows exist. Reading a break that the rule cannot explain cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A break whose source row is missing or whose procedure was mis-specified.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows which break is a bad input and which is a real change in the book.

ambition.what: A break is interpreted the morning the refresh shows it, not only in the monthly pack.

tasks.altitude: Refreshes are waiting. The analyst still interprets the break and can refuse a tie that does not match. Decision rights on the reading do not move.

reach.task: Say which result breaks change an insurance price
reach.learn: Which unexplained breaks an underwriter will ask about

evidence.claim: A tool pulls source evidence and runs a test of details, and the team reviews and signs off.
In a published spreadsheet-agent test, most models ended a cash waterfall at €1.16 million, not €580,000.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. Boundary: from a procedure result to a recorded interpretation. Changing the procedure is a later task.

Structured fields are procedure id, result, source row and tie status. The procedure produces the result; the source system produces the row. Fallback: a result with no source row is not recorded as tied.
Configure the refresh on {BI} before custom code.
Upkeep of 4 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new procedure added to the refresh.
unknowns: Whether procedures already write a source row id.
Whether the monthly pack is the only reader of the interpretation.
research_questions: What share of results tie without a break?
How often is an interpretation different from the tolerance flag?

incremental.description: Add a procedure to the refresh list

approvals.approved_version: interpretation the analyst recorded against the tied results

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: source rows are missing, so the tie is done by hand and the interpretation is unchanged. High: rows are present and only the refresh shrinks. The interpretation stays.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose an econometric routine and accept it into the libraries.

steps.what: Choose the econometric technique the model libraries must hold.
Implement the quantitative routine in the model libraries.
Check the statistical result on a known series.
Accept the library routine when its stored test passes.

tasks.design: The analyst chooses the econometric technique and implements the quantitative routine. A colleague checks it on a known series. Acceptance into the model libraries stays with the analyst and requires the stored test.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routines were copied between files, so a known-series test was not kept with the code.
tasks.enabler_now: A stored test can be rerun once the routine and the series exist. Choosing the technique, and accepting the routine, cannot.
tasks.still_hard: An econometric method the known series cannot show.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows when a failed test is a wrong method rather than a bad series.
tasks.altitude: Implementation still takes most of the week. The test is kept with the routine. The analyst can refuse a routine whose test does not pass. Decision rights on the library do not move.

reach.task: Say which statistical methods a regulatory disclosure may cite
reach.learn: Which library routines are allowed in a disclosure

evidence.claim: Building a quantitative library routine and judging its method stay with the analyst.
A colleague's check of a known series is that colleague's time, not the analyst's.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. The colleague's check is not the analyst's saving. Boundary: from a library gap to an acceptance. Using the routine on a live book is later.

Structured fields are technique, series id, expected value and test status. The analyst writes the technique; the known series produces the expected value. Fallback: a routine with no stored test is not accepted.
Configure the test runner on {DATA_PLATFORM} before custom code.
Upkeep of 7 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new series added to the library tests.
unknowns: Whether a known series with an agreed value exists for this technique.
Whether the colleague is available before acceptance.
research_questions: What share of routines already have a stored test?
How often does the peer note change the technique?

incremental.description: Add a known series to the library tests

approvals.approved_version: library acceptance for the routine whose stored test passed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: no known series exists, so implementation and acceptance stay fully manual. High: the series exists and only the rerun of a finished routine shrinks. The technique choice stays. The colleague's time is not saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still choosing a technique, reading a break and deciding what a tool must measure. Series, ties and stored tests are ready before that reading. The analyst can refuse a number that does not tie to a source.
reach: Regulatory affairs specialists: say which regulation questions a stored formula must not answer
Insurance underwriters: say which unexplained result breaks change an insurance price
Personal financial advisors: say which attribution figures may be repeated outside the desk
skills_to_grow: Tying a formula result to the series it used
Reading a break a tolerance cannot explain
Refusing a library routine whose stored test does not pass
role.ambitious_version: Every filed valuation names its technique and its series, every new tool has a known-book test, and a break is interpreted before it is recorded.
